chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Saeed ibn Janaah, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) complained to his Lord (the Exalted) about the dampness and humidity, so Allah (the Exalted) commanded that he take the Halilaj, the Bililaj, and the Amlaj, knead them with honey, and take them. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is what you call Al-Tarifil.'

key_terms.الطَّرِيفِلَ: The local name for the fruits mentioned
key_terms.الْبِلَّةَ: Dampness or moisture in the body

ai.seo_question: What remedy did God prescribe for Musa (AS) to relieve dampness and humidity?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the Shia tradition of linking prophetic wisdom with practical medicine, where Prophet Musa (AS) was divinely guided to treat bodily dampness using a specific herbal remedy. The identification of the obscure terms Halilaj, Bililaj, and Amlaj as 'Tarifil' (likely myrobalan) highlights the continuity of medical knowledge transmitted through the Imams. It underscores the concept that divine revelation often includes not just spiritual guidance but also holistic care for the physical body, a theme resonant with the Imams' own extensive medical treatises.

en.hubeali: H 14676 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Saeed Bin Janaah, from a man, who has narrated the following:

Abu Abdullahasws said that: ‘Musa Bin Imranas complained to hisas Lordazwj the High about the moisture and the humidity. So Allahazwj the high Commanded that heas should take the myrobalan (fruit) and ‘Al-Balaylaj’ and ‘Al-Amlaj’, knead it in honey and take it’. Then Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘It has been named as ‘Al-Tarayfil’ among you’.
en.sarwar: 228. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Saeed Bin Janaah, from a man, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said that:

‘Musa Bin Imran (as) complained to his (as) Lord (azwj) the High about the moisture and the humidity. So Allah (azwj) the high Commanded that he (as) should take the myrobalan (fruit) and ‘Al-Balaylaj’ and ‘Al-Amlaj’, knead it in honey and take it’. Then Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said: ‘It has been named as ‘Al-Tarayfil’ among you’.
